    <div>
      <h1>Our Escalation and Autonomy Ladder (L1-L4)</h1>
      <p class="ws-sub">The published ladder: how much an agent may decide unsupervised, who is paged when it stops, and where that is logged. Pinned into the orchestration runbook.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="ws-meta">
      <b>WS-17-escalation-autonomy-ladder</b><br>
      Pack E &middot; fill order <b>6</b> &middot; rubric<br>
      format <b>A3 landscape</b> &middot; side 1 of 3<br>
      audience <b>eng-leader</b>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-source">
    Source: <b>Multi-Agent Orchestration</b> &middot; <i>The Escalation Protocol</i> &middot;
    <code>handbook/ch17-multi-agent-orchestration.qmd</code> L340-357 &middot;
    <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch17-multi-agent-orchestration.html#sec-multi-agent-escalation">#sec-multi-agent-escalation</a>
    &middot; requires <code>WS-16-consequential-effect-register</code> completed first
  </div>

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    You hold the pen. The grey columns are the book's four levels, left as printed. Write our own trigger, response and a real
    incident from our own delivery in columns 7-9, one line each, because this side gets read at three in the morning. Then name who is
    paged, the response window, and where the escalation is logged. Higher autonomy means <i>different</i> human involvement, not
    less. Do not copy the book's examples into column 9.
  </div>

  <div class="ws-block">
    <h2>Block A &mdash; the ladder <span class="ws-block-note">one row per level; four rows, fixed. Fill left to right.</span></h2>

          <th><span class="fno">7</span> Our trigger</th>
          <th><span class="fno">8</span> Our response</th>

          <th><span class="fno">12</span> Authority to approve a scope change</th>
          <th><span class="fno">13</span> Where the escalation is logged</th>
          <th><span class="fno">14</span> Consequential effects that must resolve here or above</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr>

          <td class="locked">Agent hits a test failure it can debug</td>
          <td class="locked">Agent fixes and continues</td>
          <td class="locked">Type error in generated code</td>

          <td class="locked">Agent missed 3 of 12 files in scope</td>

    <p style="font-size:7.4pt;color:#454f59;margin:2mm 0 0">
      Column 5: "The L1 and L2 levels are automated. L3 and L4 require human judgment." (ch17 L353). Column 6 sources: case study APM L125-131.
      Columns 10-13: case study APM L125-131. Column 12 is printed on the L4 row only: the person who can say yes to work outside the plan.
      Name a person or a named rota position, not "the tech lead". Column 14: carry across from <code>WS-16-consequential-effect-register</code>
      column 25: every judgement-external gate lands at L3 or L4, with the same owner. Column 6 is printed, not reconciled: the case study and the
      chapter number the middle of the ladder slightly differently, so you see both.
    </p>

  <div class="ws-foot-quote">
